e: Thiersch wiring: encirclage (purse-string) of anal canal for rectal prolapse.
Post-MRM (axillary clearance) arm swelling = lymphedema (commonest cause).
Direct inguinal hernia → tension-free mesh repair (Lichtenstein).
Tension pneumothorax (RTA, ↓ air entry, hypotension) → immediate needle decompression at 5th ICS, mid-axillary line.
Bilateral RLN palsy → both cords adducted → stridor/airway obstruction after total thyroidectomy.
CEAP: C2 = varicose veins; suffix A = asymptomatic (S = symptomatic).
Antral Ca c̅ liver metastasis is incurable → palliative gastrojejunostomy to relieve outlet obstruction.

Lingual nerve lies close to the deep part/hilum of submandibular gland → injured c̅ gland surgery.
(Marginal mandibular & hypoglossal also at risk.)
Low-risk disease (Gleason 6, PSA <10) in an 85-yr-old c̅ limited life expectancy → active surveillance.
CBD stone >2 yrs after cholecystectomy = primary (de novo) stone; <2 yrs = retained.
Free gas under diaphragm = hollow viscus perforation.
Blunt abdominal trauma c̅ hypotension = unstable → bedside FAST (not CT).

Straddle injury c̅ meatal blood = urethral injury; no blind Foley → suprapubic catheter drains urine.
RGU defines the injury later.
Dilated central small-bowel loops c̅ air-fluid levels = intestinal obstruction.
CHPS: persistent vomiting loses HCl → hypochloremic, hyponatremic (hypokalemic) metabolic alkalosis.
Verrucous Ca of glans, N0 → partial penectomy c̅ adequate margin.
Needle driven into bone c̅ tubing = intraosseous access for emergency IV fluids/drugs.
Fournier's gangrene = polymicrobial (mixed aerobic + anaerobic) necrotizing infection; Rx wide debridement + antibiotics.

IMA ligation → injury to sympathetic (superior hypogastric plexus) → retrograde ejaculation + bladder dysfunction.
Parasympathetic (nervi erigentes) injury → impotence.

Scar growing beyond original wound margins = keloid.
Hypertrophic scar stays within margins.
Lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh entrapment → meralgia paresthetica (anterolateral thigh pain).
GCS: E2 (pain) + V3 (inappropriate words) + M4 (withdrawal) = 9.
Hydatid cyst (Echinococcus granulosus): septated cystic liver lesion; fever/jaundice from biliary rupture.
Alcohol/cirrhosis c̅ weight loss + AFP 600 ng/mL (>400) = hepatocellular carcinoma.
Chronic pancreatitis c̅ dilated duct (≥7 mm) + stones → longitudinal pancreaticojejunostomy (Puestow).

ER positive = good prognostic factor (hormone-responsive).
BRCA-1, p53, high Ki-67 = poor.
Tearing chest pain to back + widened mediastinum + arm BP differential = aortic dissection.
Small (<5 cm) amoebic liver abscess after diarrhea → medical therapy (metronidazole).
Crescent-shaped hyperdense collection c̅ midline shift in alcoholic c̅ head injury = subdural hemorrhage.
Necrotizing fasciitis: repeated radical debridement + antibiotics; hyperbaric O2 is an adjunct, so 'no role' is false.
Direct hernia: weakness of posterior wall of Hesselbach's triangle (conjoint tendon/transversalis fascia).
Vibration white finger from pneumatic drills/machinery = secondary Raynaud's.
Juvenile (retention) polyp: mucus-filled dilated glands = hamartoma; painless bleeding/prolapse in child.
Painless punched-out ulcer c̅ callus on pressure point of sole = trophic (neuropathic) ulcer.

CEAP: C4a = pigmentation or eczema.
C4b = lipodermatosclerosis/atrophie blanche.
SAH on CT → angiography (CTA/DSA) next to locate aneurysm for clipping/coiling.
Alkali corrosive injury c̅ complete dysphagia → feeding jejunostomy first; reconstruction later.
Midline neck swelling moving c̅ swallowing AND tongue protrusion = thyroglossal cyst.
qSOFA: SBP ≤100, RR ≥22, altered mentation (GCS <15).
Neoadjuvant chemo = given before radical surgery to shrink tumour bulk.
Aspirin use c̅ epigastric pain + hematemesis → bleeding peptic ulcer.
Slow-growing mobile swelling below & behind ear lobule = parotid tumour (pleomorphic adenoma).
Circumferential full-thickness limb burn → long linear incision through eschar = escharotomy.
Tract between internal and external sphincters = intersphincteric fistula (commonest Parks type).
Surgeon's knot: double throw on first loop, single on second → less slippage.
Peau d'orange c̅ diffuse breast skin thickening = inflammatory carcinoma (T4d).
Varicose veins (chronic venous insufficiency) → lipodermatosclerosis, eczema, venous ulcer.
Polydioxanone (PDS) = synthetic absorbable monofilament suture.
Pinpoint preputial opening c̅ ballooning on micturition = phimosis.
Splayed carotid bifurcation (lyre sign) c̅ vascular mass = carotid body tumour.
Extra-axial, dural-based, well-circumscribed mass = meningioma.
Petechial hemorrhages in corpus callosum after RTA = diffuse axonal injury (shear injury).
Pheochromocytoma pre-op: α-blockade first c̅ phenoxybenzamine; β-blocker only after.
IVC lies behind duodenum → injury causes massive retroperitoneal bleed.
Wet gangrene: moist, swollen, infected tissue c̅ blistering/foul discharge and no demarcation.
Anal canal below dentate line (near anal opening) drains to superficial inguinal nodes.
